files.role: Public datatype facade, canonical blob layout declarations and structural classifiers, Arrow/logical-string conversion, dictionary metadata equality, and blob-kind numeric codes. Private field/schema submodules expose selected types through this facade. Layout declarations specify shapes and documented meanings; they do not themselves validate row values or implement IO.
ranges: SPDX, module description and imports establish Arrow types, shared/lazy values, deep-size accounting and bfloat16 extension helpers. Private field and schema modules re-export the explicitly listed public types/functions/constants. Field-facing exports include comparison modes, blob version, encoding and metadata keys; schema-facing exports include projections, blob handling, field-path parsing/formatting and fixed-size-list dimension validation. The exported schema implementation is analyzed separately at rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:1-3225; these declarations alone do not establish its behavior.

Legacy blob descriptor is a lazily constructed Struct of position:UInt64 and size:UInt64, both nullable. BLOB_DESC_FIELD names it description, makes the outer Arrow field nullable, and sets BLOB_META_KEY to true. BLOB_DESC_LANCE_FIELD converts that Arrow field with try_from(...).unwrap(); the initializer assumes its built-in shape remains convertible. BLOB_DESC_TYPE clones the lazily built Fields. These are frozen legacy shapes, not a new writer design boundary.

V2 logical minimal fields are ordered data:LargeBinary nullable and uri:Utf8 nullable. Complete logical fields append nullable position:UInt64 and size:UInt64. Documentation requires each non-null logical row to choose exactly one of data/uri, limits position/size to external-object ranges, and says provided range size must be positive. These statics declare Arrow shapes only; no row exclusivity/range validation occurs here. BLOB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE wraps the complete four-field layout in Struct.

Writer-prepared v2 fields have fixed order kind:UInt8, data:LargeBinary, uri:Utf8, blob_id:UInt32, blob_size:UInt64, position:UInt64, all nullable. Comments distinguish Inline carrying data, Packed carrying id/position/size, Dedicated carrying id/size with position0, and External carrying URI, optional id and range information. External blob_size0 denotes whole-object length resolved on read. blob_size prevents confusion with logical range size; stored descriptor renames uri to blob_uri. BLOB_V2_PREPARED_TYPE is the Struct of these fields; runtime routing/length resolution is not implemented here.

The source explicitly declares the stored descriptor field names part of the stable file format. Stored v2 descriptor fields, in order, are kind:UInt8, position:UInt64, size:UInt64, blob_id:UInt32, blob_uri:Utf8; all five children are non-nullable. Comments define Inline main-file out-of-line range, Packed shared sidecar range, Dedicated whole raw sidecar with position0, External URI/id plus optional range and size0 whole-object resolution. BLOB_V2_DESC_FIELD has name description, non-nullable outer field, BLOB_META_KEY=true and lance-encoding:packed=true. Its Lance Field conversion unwraps. These declarations and comments do not prove a release/version gate or that every writer enforces all meanings.

Public non-exhaustive BlobV2Layout has Logical, Prepared and Descriptor. classify(&Fields)->Option<Self> first recognizes logical forms, then prepared with strict child nullability, then descriptor ignoring child nullability. Comparisons ignore metadata throughout. The descriptor exception is documented for released schemas that represented null blobs using nullable kind versus parent struct validity. It is a structural classifier, not a data-value validator or an extension-name check.

BlobV2Layout Display emits logical, prepared or descriptor. Private blob_v2_field_matches compares exact name and DataType and optionally nullability, ignoring metadata. blob_v2_fields_match requires equal child count and ordered pairwise matches. Thus neither reordering nor width substitution is accepted, while arbitrary child metadata can be accepted.

Private logical classifier first checks the exact two-field minimal shape with nullability enforced; otherwise requires exactly the full four-field count and ordered names/types. In the full shape, nullable comparison is enforced only for data and uri, so position and size may be nullable or required. Deprecated public BLOB_V2_USER_FIELDS and BLOB_V2_USER_TYPE re-export the logical fields/type as aliases; they are not independent layouts.

BLOB_LOGICAL_TYPE is blob. Public LogicalType wraps a private String and derives Debug, Clone, PartialEq and DeepSizeOf; its Display writes that string. Exact internal predicates recognize list/list.struct, large_list/large_list.struct, blob and map; fixed-size-list-of-struct detection uses prefix fixed_size_list:struct:. Public is_struct tests exact struct. These recognizers do not validate child counts or dimension values.

From<&str> for LogicalType copies text without validation. timeunit_to_str maps Second/Millisecond/Microsecond/Nanosecond to s/ms/us/ns. is_supported_fixed_size_list_child rejects List, LargeList and Map; allows Struct only when not nested inside another fixed-size list; recurses into FixedSizeList with nested=true; all other DataType variants pass this structural precheck and may still fail later conversion. Immediate fixed-size-list Struct is allowed, nested fixed-size-list Struct is not.

parse_timeunit accepts only s/ms/us/ns and otherwise returns Error::arrow. Arrow-to-LogicalType uses Error as its associated error. Primitive spellings are null, bool, int8/uint8 through int64/uint64, halffloat/float/double; decimal strings encode bit width, precision and scale. Utf8View normalizes to string, BinaryView to binary; normal/large string and binary remain distinct. Date32/Date64 encode day/ms; Time32/Time64 use time32/time64:unit. This arm does not validate whether an arbitrarily constructed Time32/Time64 has an Arrow-valid unit; inverse conversion recognizes only the listed valid literal units at rust/lance-core/src/datatypes.rs:421-454.

Timestamp encoding is timestamp:unit:timezone; absent timezone uses -, present timezone text is verbatim. Duration uses duration:unit; Struct uses struct. Dictionary first converts value and index types, constructs dict:value:index:false, then immediately parses the result back through DataType::try_from. Failure becomes Error::schema explaining the type/string does not parse back, preventing a later Field::data_type unwrap on strings that embed unrepresentable colon-separated components or child-dependent types. The check is parse success, not exact Arrow identity (views normalize). List/LargeList distinguish a Struct element with .struct suffix; they do not inline the child logical type. View normalization is explicit at rust/lance-core/src/datatypes.rs:337-340.

FixedSizeList with a bfloat16-marked child uses fixed_size_list:lance.bfloat16:size, deliberately retaining the extension namespace to avoid collision with a future non-identical built-in bfloat16 type. Other children first pass the structural support check, then recursively encode their logical string followed by size. Immediate struct children are represented using separately retained Field children, as implemented in rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:1207-1231. FixedSizeBinary uses fixed_size_binary:size. No positivity check is performed here. Map with keys_sorted=true is rejected with a schema error because Python Arrow loses that flag; false becomes map. Other unsupported Arrow types return a descriptive schema error. Map entries validation belongs to Field conversion, not this match.

LogicalType-to-Arrow conversion directly matches the primitive spellings, valid Time32 seconds/milliseconds, valid Time64 microseconds/nanoseconds and all four duration units. blob and json both become LargeBinary. Bare struct/list/map need Field children and are not handled by this literal conversion. The inverse returns Arrow types, not original view representations or arbitrary field metadata.

Fallback splits the string on colon. fixed_size_list requires at least three parts, parses the final part as i32 and rejoins all middle parts to support nested logical strings. The bfloat16 extension name creates nullable item:FixedSizeBinary(2) with ARROW extension name and empty extension metadata; other children recursively parse and become a nullable field named item. Original child names/nullability/metadata are not recovered by this string alone. Parse errors become schema errors; negative/zero list sizes are not rejected here.

fixed_size_binary requires exactly two parts and an i32 size; invalid integer/part count yields schema error, but size positivity is not checked. dict requires exactly four colon-separated parts, recursively parses value from part1 and index from part2, and constructs Dictionary(index,value). Part3 is ignored: parser does not validate that it is false or even a boolean. Colon-containing component types cannot fit this four-part grammar. No integer-only dictionary-key validation is performed in this parser.

decimal requires exactly four parts and parses bit width as i16, precision as u8, scale as i8, reporting each parse failure as schema error. Width128/256 selects Decimal128/Decimal256; other widths yield a descriptive unsupported-decimal error. Arrow semantic precision/scale bounds beyond these integer representations are not checked here.

timestamp requires at least three parts, parses the unit with parse_timeunit and rejoins every remaining timezone fragment with colon, preserving offsets such as +08:00. Exactly - maps to None; every other string, including an empty string, becomes Some without timezone validation. Consequently a deliberately supplied Some(-) cannot remain distinct from None through this grammar. Unsupported logical text yields Error::schema, while unsupported timestamp unit comes from Error::arrow. These are source-derived edges, not all covered by tests below.

Public Dictionary derives Debug, Clone, Default and exposes offset:usize, length:usize, values:Option<ArrayRef>. Its DeepSizeOf implementation delegates to the loaded values' deep children when Some and returns0 when None, with the supplied shared accounting context; it does not add its inline offset/length storage as children.

Dictionary PartialEq compares Arrow array values when both sides are loaded, ignoring their offsets/lengths; if both values are None, equality requires matching offsets and lengths; mixed loaded/unloaded is false. Comments explain why incoming write dictionaries with zero placement should equal persisted loaded dictionaries at real offsets, while unloaded equality must remain reflexive. This equality affects schema dictionary comparison when enabled.

Public repr(u8) BlobKind encodes Inline=0, Packed=1, Dedicated=2, External=3. Documentation describes External blob_id0 as absolute URI, id>0 as URI relative to manifest.base_paths[blob_id], and optional range position default0. TryFrom<u8> accepts only0..3 and otherwise returns Error::invalid_input_source wrapping the unknown numeric value in its message. The conversion classifies kind only; it does not resolve URI, inspect id, or validate payload/range fields.

Private tests import Arrow arrays/schema and rstest. dict builds a loaded StringArray dictionary with requested offset/length. Eight parameterized equality cases cover default reflexivity, equal unloaded placement, differing unloaded offset or length, equal/different loaded arrays, loaded-versus-unloaded, and loaded equality despite placement differences. Each case asserts both comparison orders; these are source assertions, not executed results.

test_manifest_derived_dictionary_schemas_compare_equal constructs a dictionary field with values=None, offset12, length2, clones its schema, enables dictionary comparison and asserts compare true/explanation None. Despite the manifest-oriented name/comment, this test does not serialize or load a historical manifest fixture; it models its unloaded metadata in memory.

Blob classifier test asserts both minimal and complete logical layouts classify Logical, prepared classifies Prepared and stored descriptor classifies Descriptor. It checks declared shapes, not logical row content or writer output.

Structural-contract test accepts required position/size in full logical input, accepts prepared child metadata, and accepts descriptor children made nullable. A descriptor whose size child becomes UInt32 is rejected. Together these assertions pin metadata/nullability exceptions and exact numeric width, but do not validate actual null row representations.

Timestamp roundtrip parameterization covers four units without timezone plus UTC, a named region and positive/negative offsets including colon-separated forms. It converts Arrow type to logical string and back and asserts exact type equality. No timezone validity service or locale conversion is involved.

Dictionary value roundtrip cases cover string/binary, large variants, Int32, Float64 and Utf8View/BinaryView. Expected value types explicitly normalize view variants to their base types while retaining the UInt32 key; parse-back validation therefore promises representability, not lossless view identity.

Dictionary index roundtrip parameterization spans all eight signed/unsigned integer key types with Utf8 values and asserts equality after logical encoding/decoding. These fixtures do not establish rejection of non-integer yet parseable dictionary key types.

Dictionary rejection cases cover colon-bearing/child-dependent values: decimal, date, time, timestamps with/without offset, duration, fixed-size binary, nested dictionary, struct and list. Additional invalid index cases use decimal and dictionary. All assert a schema error containing does not parse back, pinning the early guard rather than waiting for Field::data_type to panic.

Timestamp encoding assertions pin exact strings for absent/named/offset timezones, including the - sentinel. Direct parser cases assert the inverse for named and offset forms. Case arrays retain exact expected spelling and unit; joining timezone fragments after the second colon is essential.

Field roundtrip checks a timestamp with +08:00 through Lance Field and back to ArrowField. Schema roundtrip checks offset and named timezone fields together. These exercise child-independent logical strings through higher-level conversion, but do not substitute for complete schema implementation review.

Four invalid timestamp strings (bare prefix, missing timezone, unknown unit with named/offset timezone) assert only that parsing fails. This file has no BlobKind invalid-byte test or general value-level blob invariant test. Tests were read in full but not run; caller-level validation, format-version gates and on-disk encoding remain outside this file.
files.limits: All declarations and tests in this file were read. Local interaction: Field uses these layouts and conversions and can unwrap the inverse (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:170-195); dictionary logical conversion therefore probes parseability (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes.rs:354-370). Schema implementation is now separately analyzed at rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:1-3225. Arrow extension helpers, downstream blob writer/reader behavior, current writer emission/version gates and whole-repository callers remain pending. No runtime tests were executed. Public statics/enum variants are schemas or documented semantics, not proof of value validation.
